request: Do task P3-18 in docs/PLAN-PHASE-3.md: 'Offline states, and a test that actually goes offline'. Follow docs/AGENT-WORKFLOW.md and read the docs in the task's Reads column (UX-PRINCIPLES.md section 7, ARCHITECTURE.md section Progressive enhancement and offline) before changing anything. A saved garden must work with no connection; a plant or a tile that is not cached says 'needs connection' rather than guessing; user-visible strings only in src/i18n/. Add a Playwright test that drives the app with the network cut. The work is done when the phase's acceptance criteria hold: npm run check, pwsh scripts/verify.ps1 and the Playwright suite (npm run test:e2e) each pass, as separate gates, as in CI.

task.title: Update ResultsSection and ResultCard to render partial offline state
task.action: In src/app/results/ResultsSection.tsx, replace Promise.all with Promise.allSettled (or per-shard try/catch) so that successfully loaded shards render normally and failed shards show a 'needs connection' placeholder. Only show the full-page error if ALL shards failed. In src/app/results/ResultCard.tsx, add an onError handler to the tag that replaces it with a PlaceholderIcon and the localized 'needs connection' string. The placeholder must be rendered from the DataError/no-data path, not by substituting a default plant or stale tile value.
task.motivation: Currently one failed shard causes a full-page error hiding all plants. The img tag shows a broken-image icon when offline. The task requires per-item placeholders: cached items render normally, uncached items show 'needs connection'. The fail-closed principle (ARCHITECTURE.md) requires that the placeholder is the user-visible form of the DataError/no-data path, never a guessed value.

plan.title: Refactor catalogue and tile loaders for partial-failure handling
plan.action: In src/data/catalogue.ts, replace the throw-on-first-failure pattern with a function that returns a discriminated union: { kind: 'ok', plants } or { kind: 'partial', plants, missingShards } or { kind: 'failed' }. In src/data/tiles/loader.ts, distinguish network failures (DataError with code 'fetch-failed' or TypeError from fetch) from other errors, and return a discriminated union { kind: 'cached', tile } | { kind: 'needsConnection' } instead of rethrowing. The offline path must still call the existing Zod-validating functions (loadPlant/loadTile), not read Cache Storage directly.
plan.motivation: Promise.all in ResultsSection means one failed shard sinks all plants. The tile loader rethrows network failures without distinction, so the UI cannot tell 'needs connection' from 'data corruption'. The architecture lens requires the offline check to live in the data layer, not components. The security lens requires that validation (Zod) still runs on the offline path.

plan.title: Verify and extend SW tile caching if missing
plan.action: Read src/sw/policy.ts and src/sw/sw.ts to confirm that tile responses (climate and soil) are cached on demand in Cache Storage with SHA-256 manifest verification. If they are not, extend the SW to cache tiles on demand. Also verify that plant images are either in the shell precache set or handled by the img onError fallback added in Task 3.
plan.motivation: The tile LRU cache is in-memory only (per-session). When the browser goes offline and the page is reloaded, this cache is empty. The SW must persist tiles in Cache Storage for the saved garden to work offline after a reload. This is the core requirement of P3-18.

dod.statement: The existing SW tests still pass after any changes
src/sw/policy.ts contains a cache-on-demand rule for tile URLs that stores responses in Cache Storage
The SW caches tile responses with SHA-256 manifest verification before storing them
The change introduces no new untrusted-input, secret-handling or authorisation weakness
dod.rubric: Trace each new or modified input path to its use. Pass only if untrusted input is validated before use, secrets are neither logged nor returned, and authorisation checks fail closed.
dod.evidence: Untrusted inputs are validated before use and fail closed: policy.ts:53-60 rejects non-GET, unparseable URLs, and cross-origin requests ('if (url.origin !== origin) return { kind: "passthrough" }'); policy.ts:77 requires a well-formed 16-hex dataVersion (isDataVersion, policy.ts:86-88) before a data route is produced; expectedSha256 (policy.ts:163-171) type-checks the manifest body and returns undefined for unlisted files or malformed digests, and sw.ts:204-213 refuses to cache when mayStore fails, no manifest exists, expected is undefined, or the computed SHA-256 (sw.ts:212-213) does not match. No secrets are logged or returned; the only stderr output is build-time sizes (scripts/build-sw.mjs:82-84). The fetch handler fails open to network (sw.ts:86), which is a degradation, not an authorisation bypass.

No duplicated logic: the only SHA-256 digest in the browser context is sw.ts:212 using policy.ts's toHex helper; other createHash uses are Node build scripts in different contexts (scripts/compile-data.mjs:251, scripts/lib/sw-shell.mjs:47). plan.title: Write Playwright offline e2e test and wire it into npm run check
plan.action: Create e2e/offline.spec.ts that: (1) serves the production build from a static server so the SW is active; (2) loads a saved garden online to populate the SW cache; (3) calls context.setOffline(true); (4) navigates to the saved garden view; (5) asserts that cached plants/tiles render normally; (6) asserts that any uncached plant or tile shows the exact localized 'needs connection' string from the i18n catalogue; (7) listens for page.on('pageerror') and asserts no unhandled rejections. Additionally, add 'npm run test:e2e' to the check script in package.json so the offline test is executed by the project's standard verification gate.
plan.motivation: The task requires a Playwright test that drives the app with the network cut. The existing e2e/serviceWorker.spec.ts explicitly defers the offline test to P3-18. npm run check currently does not include test:e2e, so the new test would not be executed by the project's standard verification gate. The task says 'green when npm run check passes' — this is insufficient unless the e2e suite is wired in.
